dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}. So, this is where you live?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Is this... a good time for a visit? I only ask because, nine times out of ten, my place is unfit for guests...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, it's nice.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, I don't think I could actually live here.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This space is too big. If I'm reading on the bed and want a drink, I'd have to actually get up and walk...

choices.text: Oh, uh... That's a good point...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I know.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wait, did you just agree with me because you think I'm old? Laziness is a habit I learned from young people, you know!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wait, scratch that. I AM young...

choices.text: You could just put a chair next to the bed to hold your snacks and drinks...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Genius!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ahem, I mean... you know this place best, so it only makes sense that you would come up with a solution.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: In that case, I'm in favor of more space. Spacious rooms are more conducive to relaxation, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sure. Is there something you want to talk about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened to those... creations of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You mean the Tzitzimimeh? Yeah, it's strange.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This realm is quite special. It's almost completely isolated from the outside world, so the malice of the stars has been greatly reduced.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's probably why they look a bit out of sorts.

choices.text: I'm almost starting to feel bad for them...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Oh, that's kind of you.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: They are born of the world's malice towards humans, but don't worry — their capacity for evil was stripped away before anything bad could happen.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Now, they're nothing more than mascots.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: By the looks of it, there are illuminated creations here powerful enough to obscure the celestial mechanisms. This must be a mystical realm...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you know?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: If you read light novels, it's obvious.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The ancient vassals in "Mirage Warriors" were able to preserve many ancient technologies and mystical arts from the preceding Age of the Three Saints, including the ability to create realms.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wait, maybe it was a true story all along!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't think so...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: W—Well, in any case, all the best novels take inspiration from real life.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Actually... What are the chances Mirage Warriors was written by one of your adepti friends?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: And the feline-headed "Higashi no Sankun" and "Nishi no Oubo" are just self-inserts?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Um... Now that you say that...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wait, does that mean you actually know some kind of cat adeptus?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh, now that I think about it... I don't think the author was an adeptus.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I've been following that novel since the beginning, and the writing has changed hands twice already. That wouldn't happen with an adeptus. They can outlast pretty much anyone...

choices.text: I suppose things are safer this way.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You're not wrong. They are born of the world's malice towards humans, after all.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But don't worry, they're harmless now. Under my control, they can't do anything bad.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh, doing nothing at all sounds pretty nice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've got a point.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Most people live no longer than a hundred years, so there's no point losing sleep over issues that will take thousands of years to solve.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, live long enough, and you learn that only a handful of things in life truly matter.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You can dedicate one tenth of your time to the important things, but when it comes to the remaining nine tenths, it's just a matter of finding ways to pass the time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, that's just a general rule, okay? Not a comment on my age!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh, I don't feel like I have that much down time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hm, I guess you're right. Maybe my life is just less interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's just like the detectives from those Fontaine crime novels — always embroiled in intrigue wherever they go.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I suppose there are people like that in real life, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In real life, we call those people, "unlucky."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Actually, crime novels only chronicle a small part of a detective's life.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Realistically, the cases only last a few days.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, who knows? Maybe they're just killing time in between important events like the rest of us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Or maybe the rest of their time is spent trying to recover from mental trauma...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, when you put it that way... Choosing to do nothing is how I recover from the trauma in my life.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Okay, I'm begging you... Don't give me that look. I can hear what you're thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "Citlali's nihilism strikes again."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, I'm fine! At my age, I don't need people fretting over me... Not that I'm THAT old, of course...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, it doesn't matter... C'mon, let's go for a walk. We should grab something to eat, too. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well? What are you waiting for? Let's get a move on!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Morning! If I hadn't stayed up all night, I never would have known you get up this early.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Good night. I'm going to keep walking around. I'm not used to a night sky without stars...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I love this kind of place. Even looking at it just makes me feel so peaceful.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's quiet and far away from the crowds, just like my place. Quite a bit tidier, though...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But don't worry — as long as no deliveries make it out this way, I won't mess the place up!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You really didn't need to go to all this effort, you know. I don't exactly get homesick. But if you're interested, there are some mysterious traditions behind these items that I can share with you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: For instance, some things shouldn't be put in boys' bedrooms, and others shouldn't be put in girls' bedrooms...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Not that you need to worry about all that. Your fate is ironclad, plus you have powerful allies. That's enough to scare away any evil entities.
